summary.one_liner: Dust is a Rust command-line disk-usage tool, a more intuitive "du" that shows which directories and files take the most space as a tree with bars.
summary.what_it_does: Dust prints a compact, sorted view of the biggest subdirectories and files under a path, sized to roughly the terminal height by default. It recurses smartly to find large entries rather than listing everything. Bars and percentages show each entry's share of the total, with shaded lines indicating parent-child hierarchy. Options cover depth limits (-d), item count (-n), apparent size vs disk usage (-s), file-only or directory-only views (-F, -D), regex include/exclude filters (-e, -v), minimum size (-z), and filesystem restriction (-x). It can also emit JSON (-j), read file lists from stdin or a file, and includes a screen-reader mode (-R). Hard links are not counted multiple times unless -s is used.
use_cases: find out what is using up disk space
locate the largest files in a directory tree
compare directory sizes at a glance
export disk usage as JSON for scripting
list files by count instead of size
notable: Shows the largest entries in a tree hierarchy so the big file hidden inside a directory is visible, not just directory totals
Smart recursion chooses the largest entries instead of a simple head-style cutoff
Config file support at ~/.config/dust/config.toml or ~/.dust.toml using long flag names
JSON output and file-list input (--files-from / --files0-from) for scripting
caveats: Snap-installed build can only access files under /home, per the README
keywords: see where my disk is used
